chunks: PWM and its characteristics. The question: What is PWM? What are its characteristics?
PWM (pulse-width modulation) controls how much power a load gets by switching a signal fully on and fully off, over and over, very fast.
The fraction of each cycle that the signal is on is the duty cycle. A higher duty cycle means more average power.
It is popular because a switch that is either fully on or fully off wastes very little energy.
Picture flicking a light switch on and off many times a second. If it is on for 30% of each cycle, your eye sees a light that is 30% as bright. Nothing in the bulb is "partly on".
It is just averaged. The load acts like a low-pass filter: it can't follow the rapid switching, so it responds to the average.
The wave spends 30% of each 1 milliseconds period high. The average (orange) is 1. 5 volts but the RMS (green) is 2. 74 volts, which matters when the load is a heater or lamp.
Notice the signal itself never sits at 1. 5 volts. Drag D toward 90%: the average rises linearly, the RMS more slowly, and the gap between them closes as the wave approaches DC.
Drag D down to 5%: the RMS is more than four times the average.
Duty cycle: ( D ): the fraction of the period that the signal is high, t on over T . Period and frequency: T is the time of one on-off cycle, and f equals 1 over T .
Average value: D times V , what a slow load responds to. RMS value: V square root of D , what matters for heating a resistor.
Low-pass filter: smooths the pulses into their average.
A 5 volts signal switches at 1 kilohertz, so the period is 1 milliseconds. It is high for 0. 3 milliseconds each cycle, so D equals 0. 3 . The average is 0. 3 times 5 equals 1.
5 volts. The RMS value is 5 square root of 0. 3 about 2. 74 volts. A heater would warm as if driven by 2. 74 volts, while a filter would output 1. 5 volts. That is the whole idea.
"PWM is switching a signal fully on and off at a fixed frequency and varying the on-time fraction, the duty cycle D . The average is D times V , for example 1.
5 volts from a 5 volts signal at 30%, but the RMS is V square root of D , which sets heating. A filter or a slow load averages it.
The main benefit is efficiency, since the switch is either on or off. Frequency is the trade-off: higher means smaller filters but more switching loss and EMI."
